item.title: A look back at Indiana’s most recent EF4 tornado in Henryville
item.description: The Henryville tornado, which was the most recent EF-4 tornado in Indiana's history, devastated communities on its 49-mile track in southern Indiana on March 2, 2012, with 170 mph winds, resulting in 11 fatalities.

item.title: Woman dies after shooting on Indy’s west side
item.description: A woman was fatally shot in the 1300 block of Sheffield Avenue in Indianapolis on Monday morning, and no arrests have been made.

item.title: Gov. Braun seeks parents’ input on new social media law
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun has urged parents to provide feedback on Indiana's new social media law, which requires social media companies to verify the ages of users and obtain parental approval for people younger than 16. He has expressed hope that the law will spur further legislation.

item.title: Indiana doctor’s license suspended after patients report sexual abuse
item.description: The Indiana Medical Licensing Board has suspended the medical license of Dr. A. Michael Guirguis for 90 days due to allegations of sexual abuse of multiple male patients during medical exams.

item.title: Fulton County man dies during raccoon hunting accident
item.description: A 31-year-old man from North Judson, Indiana, died after being struck in the stomach by a ricocheting bullet while raccoon hunting in Fulton County.

item.title: Some Arcadia residents told to evacuate after contractor hits gas main
item.description: The Jackson Township Fire Department issued an evacuation order for residents within a quarter-mile of West East Street and Howard Avenue in Arcadia, Indiana, after a gas main strike caused by an independent contractor doing fiber work in the area.

item.title: War in the Mideast widens as Trump says strikes on Iran could last 4-5 weeks
item.description: The United States and Israel launched coordinated attacks on Iran over the weekend, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of other senior figures, prompting a furious Iranian response that threatens a wider regional war.

item.title: Superintendent of Hamilton Southeastern Schools to step down
item.description: Patrick Mapes announced his resignation as superintendent of Hamilton Southeastern schools, effective April 13th, after previously serving as superintendent of the Perry Township School District for seven years.

item.title: ‘Turning tragedy to hope’: Indiana family meets Ohio toddler who received late son’s kidney
item.description: The family of Dalton Eades, a 14-year-old who died in January 2025, met the family of Luke Gingras, a 3-year-old who received one of Dalton's kidneys, before a Pacers and Grizzlies game, and the two families shared stories and photos of Dalton and Luke.

item.title: Indiana woman caught stealing endangered fish species from Patoka Lake
item.description: A woman was arrested in Crawford County for stealing an endangered species of fish from Patoka Lake spillway, in violation of Indiana's protective order.
